meta.title: feat: add segments prop to DataTableProvider
meta.body_summary: Adds optional segments prop to DataTableProvider, allowing pre‑fetched segments to be passed directly instead of always fetching on the client.

perf_labels.notes: Devin added segments prop to reduce client fetching; review feedback led to refactoring hook; merged after CI and E2E pass.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 2547 changed lines across 32 files, this is a medium-to-large edit by absolute volume, but the core change is small (only a few files in the data-table package). Most lines come from merge commits bringing in unrelated pbac feature files. As a small incremental performance optimization, it was merged after CI and E2E checks passed.

review_details.concern_detail: No explicit concerns raised in review; the formal review was approved with an empty body.
review_details.performance_claim: Passing segments as a prop reduces client-side data fetching, potentially improving page load performance by avoiding unnecessary network requests.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Simple prop addition and hook modification within a React component; Devin needed to iterate on approach (initially a separate hook vs modifying existing) per implicit feedback.

detection_detail.ci_auto: GitHub Actions ran E2E tests and reported results ready; all checks passed before merge.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: Performance claim is narrative only; no before/after timing or benchmark. E2E tests ensure functionality, not performance.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: After initial implementation, the agent refactored to modify existing useSegments hook rather than creating a new one, and fixed a failing test in slots.test.ts.

core_change_summary.description: Added optional segments prop to DataTableProvider to allow pre-fetched segments to be passed directly, and modified useSegments hook to accept them instead of always fetching via TRPC; includes type updates and test fixes.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: Most line churn comes from merge commits pulling in unrelated pbac feature files; the core optimization is contained within the data-table package.
